text:
marta: FYI I ran a perfetto + nsys trace on the KV/prefix cold-run for the 7B model after the recent kernel-selector change. Seeing a weird kernel handoff at ~3.2s where the runtime switches from fp16_fused matmul to a generic matmul and latency spikes by ~28% :thinking_face:
perf-bot: trace uploaded: https://perf.example.org/trace/1865123456 (nsys + perfetto merged)
olivia: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet or the kernel names?
marta: snippet below from the timeline view:
```
3.05s  matmul_fp16_fused_kernel_v2  grid(256,8)  time=12.5ms
3.20s  matmul_generic_fp16           grid(128,16) time=16.0ms  <-- unexpected
3.35s  kv_lookup_kernel               grid(64,32)  time=4.2ms
```
sam: that matmul_generic shows up when a fallback path is chosen due to "unsupported" sequence length pattern. Did the selector policy change thresholds recently?
olivia: I did tweak kernel selector to prefer memory-stable kernels when seqlen variance > 0.3 (commit: a4f3d7c). Might be too aggressive for short prefixes.
devin: also seeing higher L2 cache miss rate at the same window in the trace. nvprof output (aggregated):
```
Kernel             L2_MISS    L2_HIT_RATE   sm_eff
matmul_fp16_v2     1.2M        0.87         0.92
matmul_generic     3.8M        0.55         0.61
kv_lookup_kernel   0.4M        0.78         0.88
```
marta: so switching to matmul_generic knocks down SM efficiency and increases L2 misses. Could explain the latency regression.
olivia: thanks. Is this reproducible with a synthetic workload (prefix-heavy)?
marta: yes, repros in our perf harness with prefixes of length [12, 40] skewed 70/30. The selector is toggling mid-run when the observed seqlen distribution crosses the 0.3 threshold.
sam: that sounds like a batching/selector feedback loop. If batching groups mix short+long, selector flips and causes hot kernels to change mid-batch.
devin: two quick fixes: 1) increase hysteresis in selector (only switch after N batches) 2) prefer kernel pinned to batch's majority seqlen. Both should avoid on-the-fly handoffs.
olivia: I can try hysteresis first. What about cache effects? If we force the fused kernel, does KV cache warm differently?
marta: with forced_fused=true in runtime we see steady prefix hit rate 93% vs 85% before, and tail p99 token latency drops 18%. So fused kernel seems more cache-friendly here.
replay-bot: replay run queued: replay://1865123456?tag=forced-fused-hysteresis
sam: let's do a small A/B in staging: rollout selector hysteresis=3 batches for 24h and compare token cost and p99. If good, merge.
olivia: I'll push a patch to add selector.hysteresis_batches (default 1 -> 3) and a flag selector.debug_force_kernel to repro.
marta: added perf notes and nvprof snippets to the trace ticket. Linking: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RINF-5237
devin: +1. Also add a metric: kernel_switch_count per-second so we can alert on high churn.
olivia: good call. I'll add that to the runtime telemetry PR.
marta: thanks everyone, will follow up with the staging compare results tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
